transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-10
Start: 15:00 EST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Park (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Marta Gonzalez (Cedarwood - Head Cloud Ops), Raj Patel (Cedarwood - CISO), Lena Morris (Cedarwood - PM)

Summary (auto):
Quick discovery on data residency and logging constraints. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for regulated banking workloads (GDPR + HIPAA adjacent due to customer data). Primary concerns: data residency in EU/US regions, encryption/KMS, audit logs granularity and PII redaction, retention and log export restrictions, SLA for dedicated capacity, and timeline for pilot.

Topics: Data residency (EU/US), GDPR implications, HIPAA considerations, SOC2/KMS, logging and retention limits, private deployment/VPC, dedicated reserved capacity pricing, next steps for pilot.

Transcript:
00:00 Sofia (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, do you all see my screen? just to kick off, quick intros, we'll focus on your compliance questions — data residency, logging, and options between Hosted, Dedicated and Private.
00:28 Marta (Customer): yes can see, thanks. i'm marta, i run cloud ops for cedarwood. raj will lead on security. lena's joining for product context.
00:42 Raj (Customer): hi all, quick note i'm the ciso, main ask is we cannot permit eu customer data to leave eu, and logs that contain pii have to be controlled. we also need audit logs with user-level granularity and an export process for our auditors.
01:05 Ethan (Redwood SE): got it. to be clear, with Hosted we offer region pinning to EU or US, but hosted means redwood controls the infrastructure; we provide data residency guarantees in our TOS and can show SOC2 and data flow diagrams. dedicated and private give you more control — dedicated is reserved capacity in our infra in a region, private is VPC or on-prem where you control the plane.
01:32 Raj: okay, what's the practical difference for logs? we'd prefer logs not leave our env even metadata.
01:40 Sofia: good question. in Hosted we collect operational logs for monitoring and billing — those can be configured to not contain PII, and we can limit retention. we also have a compliance pack that shows what fields are redacted. for Dedicated we can route logs to your cloud logging (Cloudwatch / Stackdriver) and we can optionally disable sending certain debug traces back to Redwood's control plane.
02:05 Marta: when you say "route logs" do you mean agent on our VPC or you push logs from your service into our collector?
02:15 Ethan: depends — for Dedicated we run in our region but can stream logs to your collector via secure TLS, or for Private deployment we deploy the inference runtime inside your VPC so logs never leave. note: some telemetry for fleet health may be optional to share.
02:38 Raj: telemetry is a big one — we need to know what telemetry you absolutely need for SLA and what is optional. also we have strict retention rules for audit logs — 7 years for some records. can you hold logs for that long? and how do you handle deletion requests under GDPR?
03:05 Sofia: we can configure retention policies; for Hosted we offer X days by default but for enterprise customers we can extend retention or send logs to your archive. GDPR deletion requests are handled through our data removal workflow — we map identifiers in the service and remove associated stored artifacts; we will share the standard workflow but we can PV the process for Dedicated/Private where you have even more control.
03:35 Lena (Customer): on HIPAA — we handle some health-adjacent forms in a vertical product. would Redwood sign a BAA?
03:44 Sofia: yes, we do offer a BAA for customers with HIPAA needs on Private or Dedicated; Hosted may be possible depending on controls and our legal review. we'll include BAA guidance in the pack.
03:56 Raj: encryption — we use our own keys via KMS, must ensure customer-managed keys. is BYOK possible?
04:05 Ethan: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments and for Dedicated we have an integration path: you can bring KMS and we can use envelope encryption. Hosted supports CMK via partner integrations in some regions; we'll detail the tradeoffs.
04:30 Marta: network restrictions: we have strict egress controls and only allow connections to specific endpoints via a proxy. will that break anything?
04:40 Ethan: for Private we live inside your VPC so that's fine. For Dedicated we can support VPC peering or private endpoints, and for Hosted we provide restricted endpoints — but proxy setups can add latency and sometimes break streaming websockets; we've seen customers need to allow a small set of IPs for streaming. we'll capture your proxy requirements in the network diagram.
05:10 Raj: logging content — can you show sample audit logs? we need fields like user id, API key id, model version, prompt hash (not content) and response metadata. really cannot have full prompts with PHI in logs.
05:30 Sofia: absolutely, we'll send redacted sample logs. our standard approach is to hash prompts and only keep metadata; full prompt retention is opt-in for debug and subject to contractual limitations.
05:50 Speaker 1 (transcript noise): uh hm, sorry quick background noise, 
06:05 Ethan: also note we have KV cache references in docs — sometimes transcribed as 'KV cash' in support notes — but the cache keys are ephemeral and not stored in logs unless you enable debugging.
06:28 Marta: timeline — we want to decide on pilot approach within 3 weeks. what would a pilot look like?
06:36 Sofia: typical pilot: 4-week POC, run 2-3 templates of regulated workflows, measure latency/cost and validate audit log exports. for Dedicated pilot we may provision a small reserved pool; for Private pilot we do a quick install inside a staging VPC.
06:54 Raj: ok for the pilot we need an NDA and then a security questionnaire. we have a standard survey (30 pages) — is that okay?
07:05 Sofia: yes please send the questionnaire, we'll loop in product security. we'll also provide our security pack and SOC2 docs.
07:20 Lena: one product question, do you support function/tool-calling or structured outputs? we plan to use tool calls and ensure structured data doesn't leak.
07:30 Ethan: yes we support function-style calls, and there's options to not persist outputs, or to persist them in your customer-controlled storage in Private/Dedicated modes. Hosted can be configured to not retain outputs by default.
07:52 Raj: any limitations for GDPR on model weights — e.g., can model be trained on customer data? we do not plan to retrain, but need assurance.
08:05 Sofia: Redwood does not retrain hosted models on customer prompt data; we have an explicit policy and can contractually ensure that. for Dedicated/Private, you control the model lifecycle. we'll include language in the DPA.
08:30 Marta: SLA questions — if we go Dedicated, what's the SLA and support window?
08:38 Ethan: Dedicated comes with an SLA for uptime and latency targets; support is 24/7 for Sev1 for enterprise customers. exact numbers depend on the reservation size — we'll include a sample SLA for the 3-node reserved pool in the pricing doc.
08:58 Raj: curious about fallback behavior — if Dedicated pool is saturated do you have automatic fallback to hosted? that's a hard no for us unless regionally constrained.
09:10 Sofia: fallback is configurable — can be disabled. for strict residency requirements we would keep traffic in-region and not fall back to Hosted outside region. we'll document routing policies and can enforce no-fallback for the pilot.
09:30 Lena: how about logging restrictions for legal holds? sometimes legal requires holding data for an investigation but we can't surface it.
09:40 Ethan: in Private/Dedicated you can implement legal hold in your retention policies; for Hosted we can implement export + hold workflows but it needs contract language — we'll cover that in the security pack.
09:58 Raj: is there any component that will store raw prompts in third-party analytics (like Sentry)? we have a strict vendor list.
10:08 Sofia: we don't send raw prompts to third-party analytics; we do instrument errors with sanitized context. we can provide vetting docs for vendors we use.
10:25 Marta: can you provide an example network diagram for Dedicated vs Private?
10:32 Ethan: yes, we'll attach diagrams. Dedicated — your traffic goes to our regional infra with private endpoints; Private — runtime in your VPC, control plane optional in your account.
10:50 Raj: about encryption at rest for model weights — are they encrypted with CMKs?
10:57 Ethan: model weights are stored encrypted at rest; for Private we can use your KMS for key wrapping; for Dedicated we support envelope encryption where customer CMKs wrap service-managed keys.
11:15 Speaker 2 (ambient): mm hm
11:30 Sofia: quick note on compliance artifacts — we'll include SOC2, ISO summaries, BAA template, DPA, and a sample log export CSV.
11:45 Raj: for GDPR we need data subject access request handling — we expect Redwood to have a process to locate and remove data.
11:55 Sofia: yes, DSR process is documented; we'll include steps and SLA for DSRs.
12:10 Marta: any red flags you've seen with banks during onboarding?
12:18 Ethan: common ones: proxy/websocket issues, needing private endpoints for streaming, desire for customer KMS, strict retention and long-term archive requirements, and sometimes PCI/HIPAA contract language needing legal review. none are blockers but require timelines.
12:42 Raj: idea — can we do a quick checklist now? say yes/no to: BAA, CMK support, ability to keep logs in our collector, no fallback, sample audit log, SOC2 report, on-prem option.
12:58 Sofia: yes to BAA (subject to review), yes to CMK (Private/Dedicated), yes to log streaming to your collector, yes to disabling fallback, yes to sample logs, yes to SOC2, yes to on-prem option.
13:20 Lena: pricing — rough delta between Hosted and Dedicated for our expected throughput (approx 1M tokens / mo)?
13:30 Sofia: we'll provide a pricing estimate — Dedicated is often a fixed monthly commit and lower per-token unit costs; Hosted is pure usage-based and easier to start. we'll include a table in the follow-up.
13:50 Raj: any limitations for EU data residency when using certain third-party models or accelerators? e.g., some hardware backends zone restrictions.
14:05 Ethan: some GPU clouds have limited regional availability; our model catalog marks region compatibility. for strict EU residency we sometimes recommend Dedicated or Private to avoid cross-region fallbacks.
14:28 Marta: ok next steps recap?
14:34 Sofia: i'll send the security pack + SOC2 + BAA template, ethan will schedule a technical deep dive for Private deployment and run benchmarks, and you will send the security questionnaire and network diagram.
14:49 Raj: timeline — we aim to start pilot 3 weeks from now.
15:00 Sofia: noted, we'll target timelines in action items. any final questions?
15:10 Marta: none, thanks everyone.
15:18 Raj: thanks, appreciate it.
15:25 Meeting end.

Notes: transcription contains occasional minor errors (speaker mislabels and background noise). Refer to attached files mentioned in next steps: /security/soc2-summary.pdf (link), /security/baa-template.docx (link), /benchmarks/dedicated-3node-estimate.xlsx (link).
